content:
It's 2026 and some people still openly claim Bitcoin has no use case - a stance that has now become a declaration of the speaker's ignorance, not the technology's limitations.

I've spent some time thinking about why this still happens, and there are really only three explanations.

The first is an honest one: most of Bitcoin's highest-impact use cases are in the Global South. Remittances, inflation protection, financial access for the unbanked, resistance to monetary colonization. If you live in the West, these problems are invisible to you. They don't make your evening news. You've never had your savings halved in a year by your government's monetary policy, and nobody you know has ever paid 15% to send money home to their family. So when someone says “no use case,” what they often mean is “no use case that affects me personally.” That's a statement about their field of vision, not about Bitcoin.

The second is psychological. A lot of people who say “no use case” looked at Bitcoin at $100, $1,000, $10,000, or $50,000 and passed. The mind has a well-documented tendency to retroactively justify decisions that turned out poorly. If you missed it, the most comfortable position is that there was nothing to miss. The alternative is painful.

The third is more interesting. Bitcoin may be the first major technology in modern history where utility reached the developing world before the developed world. That's the reverse of almost every technology adoption curve we've seen. The internet, mobile phones, electricity, antibiotics, all started in the West and diffused outward. Bitcoin went the other way. It found product-market fit first among people whose currencies were failing, whose governments were seizing assets, whose banking systems excluded them. The West will be last to understand Bitcoin's utility, because the West is last to need it. That's an unusual position for people accustomed to being first.

As a technology investor, I look at Bitcoin as I do any technology: with initial skepticism followed by due diligence before making an assessment. I've probably seen thousands of technologies over the years, and been pitched hundreds of times. The result of my due diligence on Bitcoin is that only three software-based technologies stand out as genuinely transformational to society at large over the last 30 years: the Internet, AI and Bitcoin.

Like the Internet in 1994, most people aren't aware of how Bitcoin will transform society yet. So here's a list of 21 uses you probably aren't aware of that have already emerged and achieved scale.

Like the Internet, this is just the start. There will be hundreds if not thousands of other applications of Bitcoin, each one of which will make a big difference to our lives.

These are not theoretical “one day” use cases. These are real-world examples of Bitcoin being used at scale today.

21 Bitcoin use cases already working at scale

  1. Allowing refugees to re-establish a life with their savings intact (329,000 people so far impacted)
  2. Allowing hundreds of millions of people in developing nations to receive remittance payments from family without delays and without heavy fees
  3. Preventing a 50%+ p.a. family wealth erosion for people in countries with hyperinflation or high inflation (250 million+ potentially impacted)
  4. Preventing fraud and ballot tampering in Guatemala's 2023 election (17.3 million people impacted)
  5. Providing a legitimate path to re-establish economic sovereignty of 14 African nations currently experiencing French financial colonization
  6. Helping Afghan women avoid state-level financial discrimination (20 million impacted)
  7. Providing banking to the unbanked (2 billion people impacted)
  8. Providing a financial system that is harder to use for money laundering than fiat currency
  9. Having a global monetary system whose fixed monetary supply cannot prolong wars and increase wealth gaps
  10. Removing the risk of financial reprisal for running humanitarian campaigns in nations under autocratic rule (4.5 billion people potentially impacted)
  11. Allowing 4.1 million merchants (mostly small business owners) to receive payment without high Visa/Mastercard fees
  12. Enabling renewable microgrids to deliver electricity to 28K rural villagers in Africa (potential impact: 600 million)
  13. Getting aid to tens of thousands of war refugees in Ukraine, Gaza and other areas
  14. Having a secure, permissionless, decentralized, 24/7 store of value with fixed monetary supply that prevents currency debasement
  15. Reducing the time it takes utility-scale solar generation facilities to achieve ROI from 8.1 to 3.5 years
  16. Accelerating the renewable transition by increasing the profitability and reducing the curtailment of renewable generation
  17. Reducing emissions from landfills
  18. Having a monetary system with significantly lower emissions intensity than the banking system
  19. Saving 7,800 sq km of National Park in Africa (in the words of the park owner)
  20. Allowing nations such as Ethiopia to accelerate building of infrastructure to rural areas currently without electricity (affects 600 million people in Africa)
  21. Developing energy independence for nation-states, such as Bhutan

Next time you hear someone say “Bitcoin has no value”, remember that what they are actually declaring is, “My opinion on Bitcoin has no value.”
